latin: Actus quo foelicitatur natura angelica et rationalis ultima foelicitate, nec est actus intellectus, nec uoluntatis, sed est unio unitatis quae est in alteritate animae cum unitate quae est sine alteritate.
translation: The act by which the angelic and rational nature is made happy with ultimate happiness is neither an act of the intellect nor of the will, but is the union of the unity that is in the otherness of the soul with the unity that is without otherness.
translation_note: "foelicitate"/"foelicitatur" (happiness, made happy) are the classical terms for beatitude; kept as "happiness" rather than the more scholastic "beatitude" to match Pico's own vocabulary.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch13, from Latin at farmer1998:20885
doctrine: The thesis holds that the act by which the angelic and rational nature attains ultimate happiness is neither an act of the intellect nor of the will, but a union of the unity that is in the soul's otherness with the unity that is without otherness (farmer1998:20885). Farmer records no explanatory note on this thesis and no cross-reference to another (per the sources consulted).
context: Giulio Busi and Raphael Ebgi discuss the thesis as Pico's resolution of the scholastic debate over whether final beatitude consists in an act of the intellect or of the will, reporting that Pico ("il Conte") took the side of neither, holding instead that our ultimate happiness resides, in his own words, "in the union of the unity that is in the otherness of the soul with the unity that is without otherness" (busi2014:18739).
reception: Busi and Ebgi cite Pico's own discussion of the thesis in the Apologia at pp. 78-79, without giving its content in the excerpt consulted here (busi2014:18739).
historiography: Busi and Ebgi's note is the only scholarly discussion of this thesis located in the sources consulted (busi2014:18739).

not_established: The content of Pico's own defense of this thesis in the Apologia at pp. 78-79, cited by Busi and Ebgi but not itself consulted: not established by the sources consulted (busi2014:18739).
